name: User-Name
description: The user's identity, normally a Network Access Identifier. In 3GPP interfaces it often carries the IMSI. Inherited from RADIUS.

name: Framed-IP-Address
description: The IPv4 address assigned to the user's session. In 3GPP interfaces such as Gx it carries the UE's IPv4 address. Inherited from RADIUS.

name: Filter-Id
description: The name of a filter list that is configured locally on the access device, used to apply a predefined set of traffic rules to the user. Inherited from RADIUS.

name: Class
description: An opaque value that the server hands out in an answer and that the client returns unchanged in later messages of the same session, such as accounting. Inherited from RADIUS.

name: Called-Station-Id
description: The number or name the user's session was directed to. In 3GPP interfaces it typically carries the APN. Inherited from RADIUS.

name: Proxy-State
description: Opaque state that a proxy or relay adds to a request so it can recover that state when the answer comes back. The answer must echo it, and only the node that added it reads it.

name: Acct-Session-Id
description: An accounting session identifier inherited from RADIUS. Diameter keeps it mainly for RADIUS translation, since Session-Id serves the same role natively.

name: Acct-Multi-Session-Id
description: Links several related accounting sessions, each with its own Session-Id, so that records for one logical service can be correlated.

name: Event-Timestamp
description: The time, in seconds since 1900 UTC, at which the event that triggered the message occurred, such as a usage report or accounting record.

name: Acct-Interim-Interval
description: Sent by the server to tell the client how often, in seconds, to send interim accounting records. A value of zero or absence means no interim records are expected.

name: Framed-IPv6-Prefix
description: An IPv6 prefix assigned to the user's session, encoded as a prefix length followed by the prefix bits. In 3GPP interfaces it carries the UE's IPv6 prefix. Inherited from RADIUS.

name: MIP6-Home-Link-Prefix
description: The home network prefix of a Mobile IPv6 node, encoded as a one-octet prefix length followed by the 128-bit prefix. The home AAA server may allocate it or confirm one proposed by the access side.

name: Host-IP-Address
description: An IP address of the sending Diameter node, advertised in capabilities exchange. A node lists one per local address it can use for the connection.

name: Auth-Application-Id
description: Identifies an authentication and authorization application, by its application id. It appears in capabilities exchange to advertise support and in requests to say which application the message belongs to.

name: Acct-Application-Id
description: Identifies an accounting application, by its application id. It appears in capabilities exchange to advertise support and in accounting messages to say which application the record belongs to.

name: Vendor-Specific-Application-Id
description: Advertises or identifies a vendor-specific Diameter application. It pairs a Vendor-Id with either an Auth-Application-Id or an Acct-Application-Id. 3GPP applications such as S6a and Gx use it with vendor 10415.

name: Redirect-Host-Usage
description: Sent by a redirect agent to say how widely a client may cache and reuse the redirect. Values include DONT_CACHE (0), ALL_SESSION (1), ALL_REALM (2), and ALL_HOST (5).

name: Redirect-Max-Cache-Time
description: How long, in seconds, a client may keep a cached redirect from a redirect agent before discarding it.

name: Session-Id
description: The identifier of a Diameter session, which must be unique over time. Every message of the session carries it, and it normally starts with the sender's Diameter identity followed by locally chosen values.

name: Origin-Host
description: The Diameter identity (FQDN) of the node that originated the message. Relay and proxy agents leave it unchanged.

name: Supported-Vendor-Id
description: A vendor id whose vendor-specific AVPs the sender understands, listed in capabilities exchange even where no application of that vendor is advertised.

name: Vendor-Id
description: The IANA enterprise number of a vendor. It identifies the sender's vendor in capabilities exchange and qualifies application ids inside Vendor-Specific-Application-Id.

name: Result-Code
description: Reports the outcome of a request in an answer. The thousands digit gives the class: 1xxx informational, 2xxx success (for example DIAMETER_SUCCESS 2001), 3xxx protocol errors, 4xxx transient failures, and 5xxx permanent failures.

name: Product-Name
description: A free-text name of the sender's Diameter implementation, sent in capabilities exchange. It is informational and should stay the same across releases.

name: Disconnect-Cause
description: Tells the peer why the sender is closing the transport connection in a disconnect request. Values are REBOOTING (0), BUSY (1), and DO_NOT_WANT_TO_TALK_TO_YOU (2).

name: Auth-Session-State
description: Says whether the server keeps session state for an authorization session, which decides whether a session termination exchange is needed. Values are STATE_MAINTAINED (0) and NO_STATE_MAINTAINED (1).

name: Origin-State-Id
description: A value the originating node increases each time it restarts and loses session state. A peer that sees it change knows the sender's earlier sessions are gone.

name: Failed-AVP
description: Placed in an error answer to show which AVPs caused the failure. It holds copies of the offending AVPs, or of missing AVPs with a minimal value, so the sender can see what went wrong.

name: Proxy-Host
description: The Diameter identity of the proxy or relay that added a Proxy-Info entry, so that node can recognise its own state on the way back.

name: Error-Message
description: A human-readable text explaining an error result. It is for logging and troubleshooting and is not meant to be parsed.

name: Route-Record
description: The identity of a node that forwarded the request. Each relay or proxy appends the identity of the peer it received the request from, which lets agents detect routing loops.

name: Destination-Realm
description: The realm that a request should be routed to. Diameter agents use it to choose the next hop, and it is required in requests that can be proxied.

name: Proxy-Info
description: Holds per-hop state added by a proxy or relay to a request, pairing the agent's Proxy-Host identity with its Proxy-State. The answer returns it so the agent can restore that state.

name: Re-Auth-Request-Type
description: Tells the client, in a re-auth or authorization answer, what to do when the authorization lifetime ends. Values are AUTHORIZE_ONLY (0) and AUTHORIZE_AUTHENTICATE (1).

name: Accounting-Sub-Session-Id
description: Identifies an accounting sub-session within one Diameter session, used when several services are accounted separately under a single Session-Id.

name: Redirect-Host
description: A Diameter URI returned by a redirect agent, naming a node the client should send the request to instead. Several may be listed.

name: Destination-Host
description: The Diameter identity of the exact node a request is meant for. If it is absent, any suitable server in the Destination-Realm can handle the request.

name: Error-Reporting-Host
description: The identity of the node that set the error result in an answer when it is not the node in Origin-Host, for example a relay that could not route the request.

name: Termination-Cause
description: Says why a session ended, sent in session termination and accounting stop messages. Values include DIAMETER_LOGOUT (1), DIAMETER_SERVICE_NOT_PROVIDED (2), DIAMETER_BAD_ANSWER (3), DIAMETER_ADMINISTRATIVE (4), and DIAMETER_SESSION_TIMEOUT (8).

name: Origin-Realm
description: The realm of the node that originated the message. Agents and servers use it to route answers and later server-initiated requests back to the originator's realm.

name: Experimental-Result
description: Reports the outcome of a request using a vendor-specific result code instead of Result-Code. It pairs a Vendor-Id with an Experimental-Result-Code, and 3GPP applications use it with vendor 10415.

name: Experimental-Result-Code
description: A result code defined by a vendor or application, interpreted together with the Vendor-Id in the same Experimental-Result group. It follows the same class ranges as Result-Code.

name: Inband-Security-Id
description: Advertises, in capabilities exchange, which security a peer supports on the connection after the exchange. Values are NO_INBAND_SECURITY (0) and TLS (1). Its use in capabilities exchange is discouraged, with security learned through configuration or peer discovery instead.

name: DRMP
description: The routing priority of a Diameter transaction, from PRIORITY_0 (0), the highest, to PRIORITY_15 (15), the lowest. Nodes use it to decide which messages to favour under load or overload.

name: MIP-Home-Agent-Address
description: The IP address of the mobile node's home agent, assigned or confirmed by the home AAA server for Mobile IP. 3GPP uses it to signal the PGW address for non-3GPP access.

name: MIP-Home-Agent-Host
description: Identifies the mobile node's home agent by its Diameter realm and host. 3GPP uses it to signal the PGW identity for non-3GPP access.

name: CC-Correlation-Id
description: An opaque value that lets a credit-control server link a credit-control session to another related session, such as the access session that triggered it, when the two are handled by different nodes.

name: CC-Input-Octets
description: A count of octets received from the end user (uplink), expressed as a service unit inside a requested, granted, or used service unit group.

name: CC-Money
description: A monetary amount used as a service unit. It holds a Unit-Value for the amount and an optional Currency-Code that says which currency the amount is in.

name: CC-Output-Octets
description: A count of octets sent to the end user (downlink), expressed as a service unit inside a requested, granted, or used service unit group.

name: CC-Request-Number
description: A sequence number that identifies each request within one credit-control session. The first request uses 0 and each later request in the session increases it, so the server can match answers and spot duplicates.

name: CC-Request-Type
description: Says which kind of credit-control request this is. Values are INITIAL_REQUEST (1) to open a session, UPDATE_REQUEST (2) for interim reports, TERMINATION_REQUEST (3) to close it, and EVENT_REQUEST (4) for a one-shot charging event.

name: CC-Service-Specific-Units
description: A number of units whose meaning is specific to the service, such as messages or downloads, used when time, money, or octets do not fit the service being charged.

name: CC-Session-Failover
description: Tells the client whether it may move an ongoing credit-control session to an alternative server if the current one fails. Values are FAILOVER_NOT_SUPPORTED (0) and FAILOVER_SUPPORTED (1).

name: CC-Sub-Session-Id
description: Identifies a sub-session within a credit-control session, so that several separately metered services can share one Diameter session.

name: CC-Time
description: An amount of time in seconds used as a service unit inside a requested, granted, or used service unit group.

name: CC-Total-Octets
description: A count of octets in both directions combined, used as a service unit inside a requested, granted, or used service unit group.

name: Check-Balance-Result
description: The server's answer to a balance check, telling the client whether the account can cover the requested service. Values are ENOUGH_CREDIT (0) and NO_CREDIT (1).

name: Cost-Information
description: The cost of a service, returned by the server for a price query or to advise the user. It groups the amount, its currency, and an optional label for the unit being priced.

name: Cost-Unit
description: A human-readable label for the unit that a cost applies to, such as minutes or megabytes, carried inside Cost-Information.

name: Currency-Code
description: The currency of a monetary amount, given as the ISO 4217 numeric code (for example 978 for the euro).

name: Credit-Control-Failure-Handling
description: Tells the credit-control client what to do with the service when the server cannot be reached or fails to answer. Values are TERMINATE (0), CONTINUE (1), and RETRY_AND_TERMINATE (2).

name: Direct-Debiting-Failure-Handling
description: Tells the client what to do with a one-shot direct debit when the server does not answer. Values are TERMINATE_OR_BUFFER (0), where the request is buffered or the service refused, and CONTINUE (1), where the service is delivered anyway.

name: Exponent
description: The power of ten applied to Value-Digits to form a decimal amount. For example, Value-Digits 1234 with Exponent -2 means 12.34.

name: Final-Unit-Indication
description: Marks the granted units as the last ones available for the service and says what the client must do when they run out: terminate, redirect the user, or restrict access to selected traffic.

name: Granted-Service-Unit
description: The quota the server grants the client, expressed in time, money, octets, or service-specific units. It can also carry a time at which the tariff changes.

name: Rating-Group
description: Identifies a group of services that share the same rating and draw from the same credit pool, so the server can grant and track quota per group rather than per service.

name: Redirect-Address-Type
description: The format of the address in Redirect-Server-Address. Values are IPv4_Address (0), IPv6_Address (1), URL (2), and SIP_URI (3).

name: Redirect-Server
description: Gives the address of a server that the user is redirected to, typically a top-up portal, when the final granted units are used. It pairs the address with its type.

name: Redirect-Server-Address
description: The address the user is redirected to, written in the format named by Redirect-Address-Type.

name: Requested-Action
description: The operation asked for in a one-shot credit-control event. Values are DIRECT_DEBITING (0), REFUND_ACCOUNT (1), CHECK_BALANCE (2), and PRICE_ENQUIRY (3).

name: Requested-Service-Unit
description: The amount of quota the client asks the server to reserve, in time, money, octets, or service-specific units. It may be empty to let the server choose the amount.

name: Restriction-Filter-Rule
description: An IP filter rule that limits which traffic the user may still send once the final granted units are used and Final-Unit-Action is RESTRICT_ACCESS.

name: Service-Identifier
description: A number that identifies a specific service or service component being charged, with the meaning of each value set by the service provider.

name: Service-Parameter-Info
description: Extra service details that the server can use for rating, given as a type and value pair whose meaning is specific to the service.

name: Service-Parameter-Type
description: The kind of service information carried in a Service-Parameter-Info group, with values defined per service.

name: Service-Parameter-Value
description: The value of the service information whose kind is given by Service-Parameter-Type.

name: Subscription-Id
description: Identifies the subscriber that the credit-control request is for, as an identifier type plus its value, such as an E.164 number or an IMSI.

name: Subscription-Id-Data
description: The subscriber identifier itself, formatted as named by Subscription-Id-Type, for example an MSISDN or IMSI.

name: Unit-Value
description: A decimal amount made of a digit string and a power-of-ten exponent, used to express money values without floating point.

name: Used-Service-Unit
description: The quota the client reports as consumed since the last report, in time, money, octets, or service-specific units. It can split usage before and after a tariff change.

name: Value-Digits
description: The significant digits of a decimal amount. Combined with Exponent, it forms values such as money amounts.

name: Validity-Time
description: How long, in seconds, the granted quota remains valid. When it expires the client must report usage and ask for new quota even if units remain.

name: Final-Unit-Action
description: The action the client takes when the final granted units are used. Values are TERMINATE (0), REDIRECT (1) to send the user to a server such as a top-up portal, and RESTRICT_ACCESS (2) to allow only selected traffic.

name: Subscription-Id-Type
description: The format of the subscriber identifier in Subscription-Id-Data. Values are END_USER_E164 (0), END_USER_IMSI (1), END_USER_SIP_URI (2), END_USER_NAI (3), and END_USER_PRIVATE (4).

name: Tariff-Time-Change
description: The time at which the tariff for the granted quota changes. The client reports usage before and after this point separately.

name: Tariff-Change-Usage
description: Says whether reported units fall before or after a tariff change. Values are UNIT_BEFORE_TARIFF_CHANGE (0), UNIT_AFTER_TARIFF_CHANGE (1), and UNIT_INDETERMINATE (2).

name: G-S-U-Pool-Identifier
description: Identifies a credit pool that several services or rating groups share, so quota granted to them is drawn from one common amount.

name: CC-Unit-Type
description: The type of unit that a credit pool reference applies to. Values include TIME (0), MONEY (1), TOTAL-OCTETS (2), INPUT-OCTETS (3), OUTPUT-OCTETS (4), and SERVICE-SPECIFIC-UNITS (5).

name: Multiple-Services-Indicator
description: Says whether the client can handle several independently rated services in one credit-control session. Values are MULTIPLE_SERVICES_NOT_SUPPORTED (0) and MULTIPLE_SERVICES_SUPPORTED (1).

name: Multiple-Services-Credit-Control
description: The quota management container for one service or rating group in a session. It carries requested, granted, and used units, the service or rating group they apply to, validity time, final-unit handling, and a per-service result code.

name: G-S-U-Pool-Reference
description: Links a granted quota to a shared credit pool. It names the pool, the unit type, and a multiplier that converts the units into pool credit.

name: User-Equipment-Info
description: Identifies the user's device for a credit-control session, as an identifier type and value, such as an IMEISV or MAC address.

name: User-Equipment-Info-Type
description: The format of the device identifier in User-Equipment-Info-Value. Values are IMEISV (0), MAC (1), EUI64 (2), and MODIFIED_EUI64 (3).

name: User-Equipment-Info-Value
description: The device identifier itself, encoded as named by User-Equipment-Info-Type.

name: Service-Context-Id
description: Names the service-specific document that defines how credit control is applied for this service, letting the server pick the right rating logic. 3GPP charging uses values ending in @3gpp.org, such as 32251@3gpp.org.

name: Accounting-Record-Type
description: Says what kind of accounting record this is. Values are EVENT_RECORD (1) for one-time events, and START_RECORD (2), INTERIM_RECORD (3), and STOP_RECORD (4) for the stages of a session.

name: Accounting-Realtime-Required
description: Sent by the server to tell the client what to do with the service when accounting cannot be delivered. Values are DELIVER_AND_GRANT (1), GRANT_AND_STORE (2), and GRANT_AND_LOSE (3).

name: Accounting-Record-Number
description: A sequence number for accounting records within a session. Together with Session-Id it identifies a record uniquely and helps detect duplicates.

name: MIP6-Agent-Info
description: The identity of a mobility anchor, in 3GPP use the PDN GW, as an IP address, an FQDN, or both, with an optional home link prefix. In S6a APN configuration it gives the PDN GW for an APN or the one in use.

name: Service-Selection
description: The name of the service or external network that the mobility session should be tied to, in effect an APN for Proxy Mobile IPv6. Defined as a RADIUS attribute for PMIPv6.

name: PMIP6-IPv4-Home-Address
description: The mobile node's IPv4 home address in Proxy Mobile IPv6, sent by the home AAA server when statically provisioned. On the LMA side, an all-zero value asks the AAA server to assign one.

name: Filter-Rule
description: A traffic filter that says which packets match and what to do with them. It can match on direction, addresses, ports, protocols, and time of day, and an action such as permit, drop, or rate limit.

name: Filter-Rule-Precedence
description: The order in which a filter rule is evaluated relative to others. Lower values are checked first.

name: Time-Of-Day-Start
description: The start of a daily time window, in seconds after midnight, used in a time-of-day condition. If absent, the window starts at midnight.

name: Time-Of-Day-End
description: The end of a daily time window, in seconds after midnight, used in a time-of-day condition. If absent, the window runs to the end of the day.

name: Day-Of-Week-Mask
description: A bit mask of the weekdays on which a time window applies. Bit 0 is SUNDAY through bit 6 SATURDAY. If absent, every day matches.

name: OC-Supported-Features
description: Advertises the overload control features a node supports. A reacting node sends it in requests, and a reporting node returns the features it chose in answers.

name: OC-Feature-Vector
description: A bit mask of overload control features. Bit 0, OLR_DEFAULT_ALGO, means the default loss algorithm, where a node is asked to drop a percentage of traffic.

name: OC-OLR
description: An overload report sent by an overloaded node in answers. It says how much traffic to cut, for how long, whether it applies to a host or a realm, and carries a sequence number so stale reports can be ignored.

name: OC-Sequence-Number
description: A number that increases with each new overload report from the same source, so a receiver keeps only the newest report and ignores older copies.

name: OC-Validity-Duration
description: How long, in seconds, an overload report stays in force. A value of zero ends the overload condition. The default is 30 seconds and the maximum is 86400.

name: OC-Report-Type
description: Says what an overload report applies to. Values are HOST_REPORT (0) for requests sent to the reporting host and REALM_REPORT (1) for requests sent to the realm. RFC 8581 adds PEER_REPORT (2).

name: OC-Reduction-Percentage
description: The percentage, from 0 to 100, of traffic the receiver should drop compared with what it would otherwise send. 100 asks it to stop all new traffic, and 0 means no reduction is needed.

name: SourceID
description: The Diameter identity of the node that inserted the enclosing AVP, such as a peer overload report or a load report, so receivers know which node the report came from.

name: Load
description: A load report that a node adds to messages so others can balance traffic. It holds the report type, the load value, and the identity of the node the report describes.

name: Load-Type
description: Says what a load report describes. Values are HOST (0) for a Diameter server endpoint and PEER (1) for the next-hop peer.

name: Load-Value
description: A relative load figure from 0 to 65535, read like a DNS SRV weight. Higher numbers mean less load, so 65535 is idle and 0 is fully loaded.

name: User-Equipment-Info-Extension
description: An extensible way to identify the user's device. It holds exactly one typed identifier AVP, such as an IMEI, IMEISV, MAC, or EUI-64 value.

name: User-Equipment-Info-IMEISV
description: The device's IMEISV (IMEI with software version), carried inside User-Equipment-Info-Extension.

name: User-Equipment-Info-MAC
description: The device's 48-bit MAC address, carried inside User-Equipment-Info-Extension.

name: User-Equipment-Info-EUI64
description: The device's 64-bit EUI-64 identifier, carried inside User-Equipment-Info-Extension.

name: User-Equipment-Info-ModifiedEUI64
description: The device's modified EUI-64 identifier, the form used for IPv6 interface identifiers, carried inside User-Equipment-Info-Extension.

name: User-Equipment-Info-IMEI
description: The device's IMEI, carried inside User-Equipment-Info-Extension.

name: Subscription-Id-Extension
description: An extensible way to identify the subscriber. It holds exactly one typed identifier AVP, such as an E.164 number, IMSI, SIP URI, NAI, or private identifier.

name: Subscription-Id-E164
description: The subscriber's E.164 number (MSISDN), carried inside Subscription-Id-Extension.

name: Subscription-Id-IMSI
description: The subscriber's IMSI, carried inside Subscription-Id-Extension.

name: Subscription-Id-SIP-URI
description: The subscriber's SIP URI, carried inside Subscription-Id-Extension.

name: Subscription-Id-NAI
description: The subscriber's Network Access Identifier, carried inside Subscription-Id-Extension.

name: Subscription-Id-Private
description: A subscriber identifier private to the service provider, carried inside Subscription-Id-Extension.

name: Redirect-Server-Extension
description: An extensible form of the redirect server address. It holds exactly one typed address AVP: an IP address, a URL, or a SIP URI.

name: Redirect-Address-IPAddress
description: The IPv4 or IPv6 address of the redirect server, carried inside Redirect-Server-Extension.

name: Redirect-Address-URL
description: The URL of the redirect server, carried inside Redirect-Server-Extension.

name: Redirect-Address-SIP-URI
description: The SIP URI of the redirect server, carried inside Redirect-Server-Extension.

name: QoS-Final-Unit-Indication
description: An extensible form of Final-Unit-Indication. It marks the granted units as final and says what the client does when they run out, using the extended redirect address and filter rules that can also express QoS limits.

name: 3GPP-SGSN-Address
description: The IPv4 address of the access-side control plane peer of the gateway: the SGSN for a GGSN, or the S-GW, ePDG, or trusted non-3GPP access for a PGW. On Gx the PCEF reports it to the PCRF, and it can show which network serves the UE.

name: 3GPP-GGSN-Address
description: The IPv4 control plane address of the GGSN or PGW that handles the session. On Gx the PCEF sends it to the PCRF.

name: 3GPP-Selection-Mode
description: The APN selection mode for the PDP context or EPS bearer, as received in session setup signalling. It shows, for example, whether the APN was subscribed or chosen by the UE or network without a subscription check.

name: 3GPP-Charging-Characteristics
description: The charging characteristics for a PDP context or IP-CAN bearer, which select the charging behaviour to apply. It appears in S6a subscription data at user, APN, and PDP context level, and the PCEF reports it to the PCRF on Gx.

name: 3GPP-SGSN-IPv6-Address
description: The IPv6 address of the access-side control plane peer of the gateway (SGSN, S-GW, ePDG, or trusted non-3GPP access). It is the IPv6 counterpart of 3GPP-SGSN-Address.

name: 3GPP-GGSN-IPv6-Address
description: The IPv6 control plane address of the GGSN or PGW that handles the session. It is the IPv6 counterpart of 3GPP-GGSN-Address.

name: 3GPP-SGSN-MCC-MNC
description: The MCC and MNC of the network serving the UE, taken from the RAI or the serving network. On Gx the PCEF reports it to the PCRF, and on Rx the PCRF passes it to the AF.

name: 3GPP-RAT-Type
description: The radio access technology that currently serves the UE, as a coded value. The PCEF can report it to the PCRF on Gx.

name: 3GPP-User-Location-Info
description: The current location of the UE, such as a cell, service area, routing area, or tracking area identity, coded with a type field. It is reported over Gx and passed to the AF over Rx.

name: 3GPP-MS-TimeZone
description: The time zone where the UE is, as an offset from UTC in 15-minute steps plus a daylight saving adjustment. It is reported over Gx and Rx.

name: TWAN-Identifier
description: The location of a UE that attaches through a trusted WLAN access network, such as the SSID and access point identity. It is reported over Gx and passed to the AF over Rx.

name: NOTE:	AVPs marked with a supported feature are applicable as described in subclause 20.7.
3GPP-AAA-Server-Name
description: The Diameter identity of the 3GPP AAA Server that serves a user. On SLh and SLg it is part of the serving node data when the UE is attached through non-3GPP access.

name: Abort-Cause
description: Why the PCRF aborts an Rx session or reports a bearer release to the AF. Values include BEARER_RELEASED (0), INSUFFICIENT_SERVER_RESOURCES (1), INSUFFICIENT_BEARER_RESOURCES (2), PS_TO_CS_HANDOVER (3), and SPONSORED_DATA_CONNECTIVITY_DISALLOWED (4).

name: Access-Network-Charging-Address
description: The IP address of the access network node that does charging, such as the GGSN or PGW. It is sent to the AF for charging correlation and should not cross operator borders.

name: Access-Network-Charging-Identifier
description: An access network charging identifier, such as a GCID, that the PCRF sends to the AF. It names the flows that the identifier covers. With no flows listed it covers the whole AF session. The AF uses it to link session-layer and bearer-layer charging.

name: AF-Application-Identifier
description: Identifies the application service that an AF session belongs to. The PCRF can use it to pick QoS, to fill in default service settings, or to start application detection at the PCEF or TDF.

name: AF-Charging-Identifier
description: The AF's charging identifier for the session, such as the IMS ICID. It lets charging records from the session layer be matched with those from the bearer layer.

name: Flows
description: Names a set of IP flows by media component number and, optionally, flow numbers. With no flow numbers it means all flows of that media component. Reports can add the final unit action, media component status, or content version.

name: Specific-Action
description: An event about the access network bearer. In an AAR the AF uses it to subscribe, and in a PCRF RAR it says which event is being reported. Values include CHARGING_CORRELATION_EXCHANGE (1), INDICATION_OF_LOSS_OF_BEARER (2), INDICATION_OF_RELEASE_OF_BEARER (4), IP-CAN_CHANGE (6), and INDICATION_OF_SUCCESSFUL_RESOURCES_ALLOCATION (8).

name: Max-Requested-Bandwidth-DL
description: The maximum downlink bandwidth, in bits per second, for an IP flow, counting IP-layer and higher overhead. In an AAR it is the AF's request, and in an AAA it is the most the PCRF will accept. Larger values use Extended-Max-Requested-BW-DL.

name: Max-Requested-Bandwidth-UL
description: The maximum uplink bandwidth, in bits per second, for an IP flow, counting IP-layer and higher overhead. In an AAR it is the AF's request, and in an AAA it is the most the PCRF will accept. Larger values use Extended-Max-Requested-BW-UL.

name: Media-Component-Description
description: Service information for one media component of an AF session, usually taken from SDP. It carries the media type, bandwidths, flow status, codec data, and sub-components. The PCRF uses it to derive authorized QoS and flow filters for PCC rules.

name: SIP-Forking-Indication
description: Says whether an Rx session covers one SIP dialogue or several, as with SIP forking. Values are SINGLE_DIALOGUE (0), the default, and SEVERAL_DIALOGUES (1).

name: Service-URN
description: Marks an AF session as emergency or restricted local operator service (RLOS) traffic. It holds the service URN without its "urn:service:" prefix, for example "sos" or "sos.police".

name: Acceptable-Service-Info
description: Sent by the PCRF when it rejects the AF's service information. It gives the most bandwidth the PCRF would authorize, either for the whole AF session or for each media component.

name: Service-Info-Status
description: Says whether the AF's service information is final or still being negotiated. Values are FINAL SERVICE INFORMATION (0), the default, and PRELIMINARY SERVICE INFORMATION (1), used for example when the information comes from an SDP offer with no answer yet.

name: MPS-Identifier
description: Marks an AF session as a Multimedia Priority Service (MPS) session. It holds the national name of the MPS service, for example NGN GETS.

name: Sponsored-Connectivity-Data
description: Data for sponsored data connectivity on Rx. The AF uses it to name the sponsor and application service provider, enable or disable sponsoring, and set a usage threshold. The PCRF uses it to return the measured usage.

name: Rx-Request-Type
description: Why the AF sends an AA-Request. Values are INITIAL_REQUEST (0), which opens an Rx session, UPDATE_REQUEST (1), which changes one, and PCSCF_RESTORATION (2).

name: Required-Access-Info
description: Access network information that the AF wants for its session. Values are USER_LOCATION (0), for the user's location and serving network, and MS_TIME_ZONE (1), for the user's time zone.

name: IP-Domain-Id
description: Information about the IP address domain. The PCRF uses it to bind the Rx session to the right IP-CAN session when address spaces overlap.

name: GCS-Identifier
description: Marks an AF session as a group communication session that needs priority. The format of the value is not specified.

name: Retry-Interval
description: How long, in seconds, the AF should wait before it sends the same service information again after the PCRF rejects it for a temporary reason such as cell congestion.

name: MCPTT-Identifier
description: Marks an AF session as Mission Critical Push To Talk (MCPTT). It holds an MCPTT resource priority namespace from RFC 8101 and can also name the MCPTT service provider.

name: Service-Authorization-Info
description: A bit mask with the result of checking the AF's request against a background data transfer policy. Bits mean that the transfer policy is unknown (0), that it has expired (1), or that its time window has not yet started (2).

name: AF-Requested-Data
description: A bit mask of the information the AF wants the PCRF to expose. Bit 0 asks for EPC-level identities of the IP-CAN session (MSISDN, IMSI, and IMEI(SV)).

name: Pre-emption-Control-Info
description: A bit mask that tells the PCRF which media flow to pre-empt when several candidates have the same priority. Only one bit may be set: most recent added flow (0), least recent added flow (1), or highest bandwidth flow (2).

name: Extended-Max-Requested-BW-DL
description: The maximum downlink bandwidth for an IP flow in kbit/s, for values too large for the bits-per-second AVP. In an AAR it is the AF's request, and in an AAA it is the most the PCRF will accept.

name: Extended-Max-Requested-BW-UL
description: The maximum uplink bandwidth for an IP flow in kbit/s, for values too large for the bits-per-second AVP. In an AAR it is the AF's request, and in an AAA it is the most the PCRF will accept.

name: MCVideo-Identifier
description: Marks an AF session as a Mission Critical Video (MCVideo) session and holds the MCVideo service provider's name. The PCRF can use it to prioritize the session.

name: IMS-Content-Identifier
description: Identifies the IMS communication service or dialogue that an AF session belongs to. The PCRF can use it, for example, to charge different dialogues in one IMS session in different ways.

name: IMS-Content-Type
description: The kind of IMS communication service that the AF session is for. Values are NO_CONTENT_DETAIL (0), CAT (1) for customized alerting tones, and CONFERENCE (2) for a three-party conference.

name: Callee-Information
description: Identifies the callee of an AF session by the called, requested, and asserted party addresses. The PCRF can use it in PCC decisions, for example for volume-based charging.

name: NID
description: The 44-bit Network Identifier (NID), as 11 hex digits. Together with the PLMN ID it identifies a stand-alone non-public network (SNPN) in 5GS.

name: MA-Information
description: For a multi-access (MA) PDU session, the IP-CAN type and RAT type of an access that was added or released, with the action taken.

name: 5GS-RAN-NAS-Release-Cause
description: The release cause for 3GPP or non-3GPP 5GS access. It carries a 5GMM cause, a 5GSM cause, or an NGAP cause.

name: Wireline-User-Location-Info
description: The user's location on a wireline access. For cable it is an HFC node identifier. For BBF access it is a Global Line Identifier and line type.

name: Visited-Network-Identifier
description: Identifies the network the user is visiting, such as its domain name. The I-CSCF converts the P-Visited-Network-ID header it receives into an octet value that it and the HSS agree on, so the HSS can decide whether roaming from that network is allowed. The home operator chooses the encoding.

name: Public-Identity
description: An IMS Public User Identity or Public Service Identity, written as a SIP URI or a tel URI in canonical form. On Cx it names the identity being registered, located, authenticated, or de-registered; on Sh it is one of the choices inside User-Identity.

name: Server-Name
description: A SIP URI that names a SIP server. On Cx it usually holds the S-CSCF name stored in or returned by the HSS (or an AS name for PSI direct routing); on Sh it names the AS making the request.

name: Server-Capabilities
description: A group the HSS returns to the I-CSCF to help it pick an S-CSCF for the user. It lists the mandatory and optional capability codes the S-CSCF needs, and it can also list candidate S-CSCF names.

name: Mandatory-Capability
description: An operator-defined numeric code for one capability, or a set of capabilities, that the chosen S-CSCF must have. Carried inside Server-Capabilities.

name: Optional-Capability
description: An operator-defined numeric code for one capability, or a set of capabilities, that the I-CSCF should prefer but does not require when it picks an S-CSCF. Carried inside Server-Capabilities.

name: User-Data
description: An opaque XML document with subscriber data. On Cx it is the IMS service profile the HSS gives to the S-CSCF (format in TS 29.228). On Sh it holds the Sh-Data document that an AS reads, updates, or receives in notifications (format in TS 29.328 Annex C).

name: SIP-Number-Auth-Items
description: The number of authentication vectors. In a MAR the S-CSCF states how many it wants, which lets it fetch several in advance; in the MAA the HSS states how many SIP-Auth-Data-Item AVPs it actually returned.

name: SIP-Authentication-Scheme
description: A text name for the SIP authentication scheme. Values include "Digest-AKAv1-MD5" (IMS AKA, used for both AKAv1 and AKAv2 digests), "SIP Digest", "NASS-Bundled", "EarlyIMSSecurity" (GPRS-IMS-Bundled), and "Unknown" when the S-CSCF does not yet know the scheme.

name: SIP-Authenticate
description: Challenge data that the S-CSCF places in the WWW-Authenticate or Proxy-Authenticate header. For IMS AKA it is 32 binary octets: the 16-octet RAND followed by the 16-octet AUTN.

name: SIP-Authorization
description: Authorization data related to the SIP Authorization header. In a MAR that requests resynchronization it holds RAND plus the AUTS from the terminal (30 octets); in the MAA it holds the expected response XRES.

name: SIP-Auth-Data-Item
description: One set of authentication data for an IMS user. It names the scheme and, depending on that scheme, carries AKA challenge material and keys, SIP Digest parameters, or the access line and IP address details used by the bundled schemes.

name: SIP-Item-Number
description: A sequence number for a SIP-Auth-Data-Item. When an MAA returns several authentication vectors, this number shows the order in which the S-CSCF should use them.

name: Server-Assignment-Type
description: Tells the HSS why the S-CSCF sends a SAR, which controls the registration state change. Values include NO_ASSIGNMENT (0), REGISTRATION (1), RE_REGISTRATION (2), UNREGISTERED_USER (3), TIMEOUT_DEREGISTRATION (4), USER_DEREGISTRATION (5), ADMINISTRATIVE_DEREGISTRATION (8), and AUTHENTICATION_FAILURE (9). Values 12 to 14 apply only to SWx.

name: Deregistration-Reason
description: Explains to the S-CSCF why the HSS de-registers a user in an RTR. It carries a Reason-Code, such as PERMANENT_TERMINATION (0), NEW_SERVER_ASSIGNED (1), SERVER_CHANGE (2), or REMOVE_S-CSCF (3), and optional text that can be shown to the user.

name: Charging-Information
description: The addresses of the charging functions for the user. It holds primary and secondary online (event) charging function names and primary and secondary charging data function names, as Diameter URIs, so that the receiver can direct its charging requests to them.

name: User-Authorization-Type
description: Tells the HSS what kind of authorization the I-CSCF asks for in a UAR or LIR. Values are REGISTRATION (0, the default, for registration and re-registration), DE_REGISTRATION (1, when the REGISTER expiry is zero), and REGISTRATION_AND_CAPABILITIES (2, to get capabilities for selecting a new S-CSCF).

name: User-Data-Already-Available
description: Tells the HSS in a SAR whether the S-CSCF already holds the part of the user profile it needs, so the HSS can leave the profile out of the answer. Values are USER_DATA_NOT_AVAILABLE (0) and USER_DATA_ALREADY_AVAILABLE (1).

name: Confidentiality-Key
description: The cipher key (CK) of an AKA authentication vector, given as binary octets. Cx carries it in SIP-Auth-Data-Item and S6a carries it in UTRAN-Vector.

name: Integrity-Key
description: The integrity key (IK) of an AKA authentication vector, given as binary octets. Cx carries it in SIP-Auth-Data-Item and S6a carries it in UTRAN-Vector.

name: Supported-Features
description: Lets a node tell its peer which optional features it supports for the Diameter application. The vendor ID and a feature list ID together pick a feature list, and a bit mask marks the supported features. Many 3GPP applications use this AVP.

name: Feature-List-ID
description: A number that identifies one feature list when a vendor defines more than one feature list for the same application. It appears in Supported-Features together with Vendor-Id.

name: Feature-List
description: A bit mask in Supported-Features. Each set bit marks a feature that the sender supports. The application that uses the list defines each bit; the Cx bits are in clause 7.1.1 of TS 29.229.

name: Associated-Identities
description: The list of Private User Identities, as User-Name values, that belong to the same IMS subscription. The HSS sends it in an SAA, and it appears in an RTR when the de-registration affects several private identities.

name: Originating-Request
description: Marks an LIR as part of handling an originating SIP request that an AS sends for a user, so the HSS can treat it that way. The only value is ORIGINATING (0).

name: Wildcarded-Public-Identity
description: A wildcarded Public Service Identity or wildcarded Public User Identity, as stored in the HSS, that matches the identity in the request. Its syntax is in TS 23.003. On Sh it holds only a wildcarded PSI.

name: Wildcarded-IMPU
description: A wildcarded Public User Identity stored in the HSS, with the syntax from TS 23.003. On Sh it identifies the wildcarded IMPU that covers the user identity in the request or answer.

name: UAR-Flags
description: A bit mask that the I-CSCF sends in a UAR. Bit 0, IMS Emergency Registration, marks the request as part of an emergency registration. The sender clears unused bits and the receiver ignores them.

name: Loose-Route-Indication
description: Tells the S-CSCF whether it must use the loose route mechanism for the registered Public User Identities. Values are LOOSE_ROUTE_NOT_REQUIRED (0) and LOOSE_ROUTE_REQUIRED (1).

name: SCSCF-Restoration-Info
description: Registration state that the S-CSCF stores in the HSS and can get back after an S-CSCF failure. It holds the private identity, the Path, Contact, and subscription details for each registration, the registration expiry, and the authentication scheme.

name: Associated-Registered-Identities
description: The Private User Identities, as User-Name values, that are registered with the Public User Identity named in the SAR. The HSS returns it in the SAA.

name: Multiple-Registration-Indication
description: Tells the HSS in a SAR whether the registration is a multiple registration, where one public identity registers from more than one contact. Values are NOT_MULTIPLE_REGISTRATION (0) and MULTIPLE_REGISTRATION (1).

name: Session-Priority
description: Gives the priority of the session to the HSS so it can treat priority traffic first. Values run from PRIORITY-0 (0), the highest, to PRIORITY-4 (4). The CSCF or AS maps the SIP priority it receives onto these values in an operator-specific way.

name: Identity-with-Emergency-Registration
description: A private and public user identity pair that has an emergency registration. The S-CSCF returns it in an RTA so that the HSS knows which emergency registrations it kept.

name: Priviledged-Sender-Indication
description: Tells the S-CSCF whether to treat the Private User Identity as a privileged sender, for example for priority handling. Values are NOT_PRIVILEDGED_SENDER (0) and PRIVILEDGED_SENDER (1). The spelling "Priviledged" is part of the AVP name.

name: LIA-Flags
description: A bit mask that the HSS returns in an LIA. Bit 0, PSI Direct Routing Indication, shows that Server-Name holds the AS that hosts the PSI rather than an S-CSCF name.

name: SAR-Flags
description: A bit mask that the S-CSCF sends in a SAR. Bit 0, P-CSCF Restoration Indication, asks the HSS to run the P-CSCF restoration procedure. It can appear only with ADMINISTRATIVE_DEREGISTRATION or UNREGISTERED_USER.

name: Allowed-WAF-WWSF-Identities
description: The WebRTC Authorization Function (WAF) and WebRTC Web Server Function (WWSF) addresses allowed for the subscription. The HSS sends them to the S-CSCF in an SAA or PPR.

name: Failed-PCSCF
description: Identifies a P-CSCF that the S-CSCF has found to have failed, by FQDN, by IP addresses, or both. The S-CSCF sends it to the HSS in a SAR as part of P-CSCF restoration.

name: User-Identity
description: The user that a Sh request is about. It holds one of these: a Public Identity (SIP or tel URI), an MSISDN, or an External-Identifier. Other applications that reuse it, such as SCEF-related interfaces, use it in the same way.

name: MSISDN
description: A subscriber's MSISDN in international E.164 format, encoded as TBCD: two digits in each octet, low nibble first, with 1111 as a filler for an odd number of digits. Sh, S6a, SLg, SLh, and other applications use it.

name: Data-Reference
description: Names the kind of user data that a Sh request reads, updates, or subscribes to. Values include RepositoryData (0), IMSPublicIdentity (10), IMSUserState (11), S-CSCFName (12), InitialFilterCriteria (13), LocationInformation (14), UserState (15), MSISDN (17), and UEReachabilityForIP (25). Value 20 is reserved.

name: Service-Indication
description: Names a service or set of services in an AS, and the transparent repository data that the HSS keeps for it. TS 29.364 defines standardized values and data formats.

name: Subs-Req-Type
description: Tells the HSS in an SNR whether the AS starts or ends a subscription to notifications about changes in user data. Values are Subscribe (0) and Unsubscribe (1).

name: Requested-Domain
description: The access domain for which an AS asks for data such as user state or location in a UDR. Values are CS-Domain (0) and PS-Domain (1).

name: Current-Location
description: Tells the HSS whether to start an active location retrieval before it answers a UDR for location data. Values are DoNotNeedInitiateActiveLocationRetrieval (0) and InitiateActiveLocationRetrieval (1).

name: Identity-Set
description: Chooses which set of IMS Public Identities the HSS returns when an AS asks for IMSPublicIdentity data. Values are ALL_IDENTITIES (0), REGISTERED_IDENTITIES (1), IMPLICIT_IDENTITIES (2), and ALIAS_IDENTITIES (3).

name: Expiry-Time
description: The time when a subscription to notifications ends in the HSS. The AS can propose a time in an SNR, and the HSS gives the time it accepted in the SNA.

name: Send-Data-Indication
description: Tells the HSS whether to return the current user data in the SNA when it accepts a subscription. Values are USER_DATA_NOT_REQUESTED (0) and USER_DATA_REQUESTED (1).

name: DSAI-Tag
description: A tag that selects one instance of Dynamic Service Activation Information (DSAI) for the public identity. An AS uses it with the DSAI data reference to read or subscribe to that instance.

name: One-Time-Notification
description: Asks the HSS to send only one notification and then end the subscription. The only value is ONE_TIME_NOTIFICATION_REQUESTED (0). It applies only to UEReachabilityForIP (25) subscriptions.

name: Requested-Nodes
description: A bit mask in a UDR that tells which serving nodes the requested data, such as location or user state, apply to. The bits are MME (0), SGSN (1), 3GPP-AAA-SERVER-TWAN (2), and AMF for 3GPP access (3).

name: Serving-Node-Indication
description: Tells the HSS that the AS needs only the serving node addresses or names, such as the MME name or VLR number, and no other location data. The only value is ONLY_SERVING_NODES_REQUIRED (0).

name: Repository-Data-ID
description: Identifies one item of repository data by its Service-Indication and its Sequence-Number. The HSS returns it in a PUA to report the repository data version it now holds.

name: Sequence-Number
description: A version number linked to an item of repository data or other transparent data. The AS and HSS compare it to detect updates that conflict.

name: Pre-paging-Supported
description: Tells the HSS in a UDR whether the AS supports pre-paging for a terminating call. Values are PREPAGING_NOT_SUPPORTED (0), the default, and PREPAGING_SUPPORTED (1).

name: Local-Time-Zone-Indication
description: Asks the HSS for the local time zone and daylight saving time of the visited network where the UE is attached. Values are ONLY_LOCAL_TIME_ZONE_REQUESTED (0) and LOCAL_TIME_ZONE_WITH_LOCATION_INFO_REQUESTED (1).

name: UDR-Flags
description: A bit mask of extra options for a UDR. Bit 0, Location-Information-EPS-Supported, allows EPS location to be returned when CS location is asked for. Bit 1, RAT-Type-Requested, asks for the RAT type with PS or EPS location.

name: Call-Reference-Info
description: Call details for Mobile Terminating Roaming Retry. It holds a call reference number and the AS number, and the HSS copies these into the MAP Provide Roaming Number request.

name: Call-Reference-Number
description: The call reference number for a call that uses Mobile Terminating Roaming Retry, coded as in MAP (TS 29.002). Carried inside Call-Reference-Info.

name: AS-Number
description: The address of the AS that handles the terminating call, coded like the MAP gmsc-address parameter (TS 29.002). Carried inside Call-Reference-Info for Mobile Terminating Roaming Retry.

name: Calling-Party-Address
description: The SIP or Tel URI of the party that starts a session, taken from the asserted identity. On Rx the AF can send it in the AA-Request, with callee information, so the PCRF can build rules for the call.

name: Served-Party-IP-Address
description: An IP address of the served party. In charging it is the address of the calling or called user. In S6a and the SCEF monitoring AVPs it carries a static or assigned UE IPv4 address or IPv6 prefix for a PDN connection.

name: Service-Id
description: A charging string naming the service a node is providing, such as the service an MRFC hosts or an advice-of-charge service; for conferences it holds the conference ID. It sits in IMS-Information. The S6m SIR's Service-ID is a separate Enumerated AVP, code 3103.

name: Charged-Party
description: The party to be charged, such as a public user identity. For monitoring event charging it names the entity that the network charges for the event, and it is carried in Monitoring-Event-Configuration.

name: RAI
description: The Routing Area Identity of the SGSN where the UE is registered, as a text string of MCC, MNC, LAC, and RAC digits. The PCEF can report it to the PCRF on Gx.

name: Bearer-Usage
description: Tells the PCRF what a bearer carries. GENERAL (0) means nothing specific is known, and IMS_SIGNALLING (1) marks a bearer reserved for IMS signalling. Once sent, the value holds until a new one arrives.

name: Charging-Rule-Install
description: The PCRF's instruction to the PCEF to install or modify dynamic PCC rules, or to activate predefined rules and rule groups. It can also give a target bearer, activation and deactivation times, and the access for NBIFOM traffic, all of which apply to every rule in the group.

name: Charging-Rule-Remove
description: The PCRF's instruction to the PCEF to remove dynamic PCC rules or deactivate predefined rules and rule groups, named by rule or rule-base name. It can ask the PCEF to report the resource release and carry the access information an AF asked for.

name: Event-Trigger
description: Names a policy event. The PCRF sends it to subscribe to an event that makes the PCEF ask for rules again, and the PCEF sends it to report that the event happened. Values include SGSN_CHANGE (0), QOS_CHANGE (1), RAT_CHANGE (2), USER_LOCATION_CHANGE (13), NO_EVENT_TRIGGERS (14), OUT_OF_CREDIT (15), USAGE_REPORT (33), and APPLICATION_START (39).

name: Offline
description: Turns offline charging on or off. Inside a PCC rule definition it applies to that rule. At command level in the first CCR or CCA it sets the session's default offline charging method. Values are DISABLE_OFFLINE (0) and ENABLE_OFFLINE (1).

name: Online
description: Turns online charging on or off. Inside a PCC rule definition it applies to that rule. At command level in the first CCR or CCA it sets the session's default online charging method. Values are DISABLE_ONLINE (0) and ENABLE_ONLINE (1).

name: TFT-Packet-Filter-Information
description: One packet filter from a GPRS PDP context's TFT, sent from the PCEF to the PCRF. It holds the filter, its precedence, and optional fields such as ToS or traffic class, IPsec SPI, flow label, and direction.

name: QoS-Information
description: A QoS profile with a QCI, maximum and guaranteed bit rates, ARP, and APN-AMBR values. From the PCEF it carries the QoS that the UE or a bearer requested, or the subscribed APN QoS. From the PCRF it carries the QoS authorized for a bearer, a service data flow, a QCI, or an APN.

name: Charging-Rule-Report
description: The PCEF's report on the status of PCC rules. It names the rules that are active, inactive, or failed, and can carry a failure code, a final unit indication when credit runs out, or a RAN/NAS release cause.

name: Bearer-Identifier
description: Identifies one IP-CAN bearer within an IP-CAN session. The PCEF assigns it. In a CCR, the AVPs that follow apply to the named bearer.

name: Bearer-Operation
description: The kind of UE-initiated bearer event that makes the PCEF ask for PCC rules. Values are TERMINATION (0), ESTABLISHMENT (1), and MODIFICATION (2).

name: Access-Network-Charging-Identifier-Gx
description: Sent from the PCEF to the PCRF with an access network charging identifier, for example a GCID, and the PCC rules it covers. With no rule names it covers the whole IP-CAN session. The PCRF can pass it on to the AF to correlate charging.

name: Bearer-Control-Mode
description: The bearer control mode that the PCRF picks for the session. UE_ONLY (0) lets only the UE request bearer resources. UE_NW (2) lets both the UE and the network do so. Value 1 is reserved.

name: Network-Request-Support
description: Says whether the UE and the access network support bearer setup started by the network. Values are NETWORK_REQUEST NOT SUPPORTED (0), which is assumed when the AVP is absent, and NETWORK_REQUEST SUPPORTED (1).

name: IP-CAN-Type
description: The kind of IP connectivity access network the user is on. It is required at session setup and is sent again when the access type changes. Values include 3GPP-GPRS (0), 3GPP-EPS (5), Non-3GPP-EPS (6), FBA (7), and 3GPP-5GS (8).

name: QoS-Class-Identifier
description: The QoS Class Identifier. It selects a standard set of QoS traits, apart from bit rates and ARP, for a bearer or service data flow. Values follow the QCI table in TS 23.203, for example QCI_1 (1) for conversational voice through QCI_9 (9), plus QCIs such as QCI_65 (65) and QCI_69 (69).

name: QoS-Negotiation
description: Says whether the PCRF may answer one PCC rule request with authorized QoS that differs from what was asked. Values are NO_QoS_NEGOTIATION (0) and QoS_NEGOTIATION_SUPPORTED (1), the default.

name: QoS-Upgrade
description: Says whether the SGSN accepts a GGSN raising the QoS above the requested level for a PDP context. When upgrades are not supported, the PCRF must not authorize bit rates above the request. Values are QoS_UPGRADE_NOT_SUPPORTED (0), the default, and QoS_UPGRADE_SUPPORTED (1).

name: RAT-Type
description: The radio access technology serving the UE. Codes below 1000 are generic and codes from 1000 are 3GPP-specific. Values include WLAN (0), VIRTUAL (1), UTRAN (1000), GERAN (1001), EUTRAN (1004), EUTRAN-NB-IoT (1005), and NR (1006).

name: Event-Report-Indication
description: Carries event details through the PCRF. Toward the PCEF it relays an event that an access gateway (BBERF) saw, together with the related location, RAT, or trace data. From the PCEF it lists the event triggers that the PCEF wants the PCRF to subscribe to.

name: Allocation-Retention-Priority
description: The Allocation and Retention Priority for a service data flow or for the default EPS bearer. It holds a priority level and two flags: whether the flow may pre-empt other flows, and whether it may be pre-empted.

name: CoA-Information
description: A care-of address and its tunnel details, sent from the PCEF to the PCRF for mobility cases. It carries the CoA IP address and the tunnel header length and filter that go with it.

name: Revalidation-Time
description: An NTP timestamp by which the PCEF must ask the PCRF for PCC rules again. It applies only when the REVALIDATION_TIMEOUT event trigger is also set.

name: Session-Release-Cause
description: Why the PCRF is ending an IP-CAN session. Values include UNSPECIFIED_REASON (0), UE_SUBSCRIPTION_REASON (1), INSUFFICIENT_SERVER_RESOURCES (2), and two values meant for Sd only: IP_CAN_SESSION_TERMINATION (3) and UE_IP_ADDRESS_RELEASE (4).

name: Priority-Level
description: The ARP priority level, from 1 (highest) to 15. It decides whether a bearer request is admitted when resources are short, and which existing bearers can be pre-empted. Levels 1 to 8 are for services that are prioritized within one operator's network.

name: Pre-emption-Capability
description: Says whether a service data flow or default bearer may take resources held by a lower-priority flow or bearer. Values are PRE-EMPTION_CAPABILITY_ENABLED (0) and PRE-EMPTION_CAPABILITY_DISABLED (1), the default.

name: Pre-emption-Vulnerability
description: Says whether a service data flow or default bearer can have its resources taken by a higher-priority flow or bearer. Values are PRE-EMPTION_VULNERABILITY_ENABLED (0), the default, and PRE-EMPTION_VULNERABILITY_DISABLED (1).

name: Default-EPS-Bearer-QoS
description: The QoS of the EPS default bearer: a non-GBR QCI and an ARP. From the PCEF it gives the subscribed or retained default bearer QoS. From the PCRF it gives the authorized value.

name: AN-GW-Address
description: The control plane IPv4 and/or IPv6 address of the access gateway, which is the SGW for 3GPP access or the access gateway or ePDG for non-3GPP access. A separate instance carries each address family.

name: Packet-Filter-Information
description: One packet filter from a UE resource request, sent from the PCEF to the PCRF. Depending on the operation it carries the filter identifier, precedence, filter content, direction, and optional ToS, SPI, and flow label. A deletion carries only the identifier.

name: Packet-Filter-Operation
description: The UE-initiated packet filter operation that makes the PCEF ask for PCC rules. Values are DELETION (0), ADDITION (1), and MODIFICATION (2).

name: PDN-Connection-ID
description: Identifies the PDN connection that the other information in the message applies to.

name: Usage-Monitoring-Information
description: Usage monitoring control for one monitoring key. The PCRF uses it to set volume or time thresholds, and the PCEF uses it to report measured usage. It can also set a quota consumption time and the monitoring level, ask for a report, or turn monitoring off.

name: CSG-Information-Reporting
description: Sent by the PCRF to ask the PCEF to report changes in the user's CSG information to the OFCS. Values are CHANGE_CSG_CELL (0), CHANGE_CSG_SUBSCRIBED_HYBRID_CELL (1), and CHANGE_CSG_UNSUBSCRIBED_HYBRID_CELL (2).

name: Routing-Rule-Remove
description: Removes IP flow mobility or NBIFOM routing rules for an IP-CAN session. Each rule is named by its routing rule identifier.

name: Routing-Rule-Install
description: Carries IP flow mobility or NBIFOM routing rule definitions from the PCEF to the PCRF, to install new rules or change existing ones.

name: Credit-Management-Status
description: A bit mask that tells why the charging system limited or denied service for a rule or session. Bits include End User Service Denied (0), Credit Control Not Applicable (1), Authorization Rejected (2), User Unknown (3), and Rating Failed (4).

name: TDF-Information
description: Tells the PCRF which TDF should do application detection for the session. The PCEF sends it in the initial CCR. It gives the TDF's Diameter realm and host or its IP address. The PCRF then opens the Sd session with that TDF.

name: Application-Detection-Information
description: Reports that the start or stop of an application's traffic was detected, when the PCRF subscribed to APPLICATION_START or APPLICATION_STOP. It names the application and, when known, an instance ID and the detected flows.

name: PDP-Address
description: The IP address tied to an IP-CAN bearer session, such as a PDP context or PDN connection. In S6a it holds the static address subscribed for a PDP context.

name: LCS-Client-Type
description: The category of location service the LCS client requests. Values are EMERGENCY_SERVICES (0), VALUE_ADDED_SERVICES (1), PLMN_OPERATOR_SERVICES (2), and LAWFUL_INTERCEPT_SERVICES (3). On SLg it goes with a location request.

name: Location-Estimate
description: An estimate of the position of the UE in geographic coordinates and its uncertainty, coded with the shapes from TS 23.032. On SLg the MME or SGSN returns it to the GMLC.

name: Subscription-Data
description: The subscriber's full profile as the HSS hands it to an MME or SGSN, covering both EPS and GERAN/UTRAN service. It bundles identities such as MSISDN, barring and access restrictions, the UE-level AMBR, the APN configuration profile, GPRS data, trace, LCS, CSG, and many feature-specific subscription items.

name: Terminal-Information
description: Describes the user's handset. It carries the IMEI (or, for 3GPP2 devices, the MEID) together with the software version, and is sent to the HSS in location and notification procedures or to the EIR for an equipment check.

name: IMEI
description: The International Mobile Equipment Identity of the terminal as a digit string: normally 14 digits made up of the 8-digit TAC and the 6-digit serial number, optionally followed by a 15th digit.

name: Software-Version
description: The two-digit Software Version Number (SVN) that accompanies the IMEI, identifying the software revision running on the mobile equipment.

name: QoS-Subscribed
description: The subscribed GPRS QoS for a PDP context, encoded as in MAP: the octets of QoS-Subscribed and its extension values (Ext through Ext4) are joined into one octet string.

name: ULR-Flags
description: Bit mask the MME or SGSN sets in ULR to qualify the location update. Bits include Single-Registration-Indication (0), S6a/S6d-Indicator (1, set when sent by an MME), Skip Subscriber Data (2), GPRS-Subscription-Data-Indicator (3), Node-Type-Indicator (4, combined MME/SGSN), Initial-Attach-Indicator (5) and Dual-Registration-5G-Indicator (8).

name: ULA-Flags
description: Bit mask the HSS returns in ULA. Bit 0 (Separation Indication) says the HSS keeps the MME and SGSN registrations apart, and bit 1 (MME Registered for SMS) confirms the MME is registered for SMS.

name: Visited-PLMN-Id
description: The PLMN identity of the visited network, three octets holding the MCC and MNC in BCD as used in 24.008 PLMN lists; a 2-digit MNC uses a filler nibble of 1111.

name: Requested-EUTRAN-Authentication-Info
description: Request for E-UTRAN (EPS) authentication vectors in an AIR. It states how many vectors are wanted, whether they are needed immediately, and may carry resynchronization data after a SQN failure.

name: Requested-UTRAN-GERAN-Authentication-Info
description: Request for UTRAN or GERAN authentication vectors in an AIR, with the same optional parts as the E-UTRAN variant: number of vectors, immediate-use preference, and resynchronization data.

name: Number-Of-Requested-Vectors
description: How many authentication vectors the MME or SGSN is willing to accept in the answer.

name: Re-Synchronization-Info
description: RAND concatenated with AUTS, sent when the USIM rejected a challenge because of a sequence number mismatch so the HSS/AuC can resynchronize before generating fresh vectors.

name: Immediate-Response-Preferred
description: A presence-only marker (its value is ignored) meaning the requested vectors are needed for immediate use. The HSS may use it to decide how many vectors to fetch from the AuC and return.

name: Authentication-Info
description: Container in the AIA for the authentication vectors the HSS generated, which can be any number of E-UTRAN, UTRAN, or GERAN vectors.

name: E-UTRAN-Vector
description: One EPS authentication vector: RAND, XRES, AUTN, and KASME, with an optional Item-Number that orders it among the returned vectors.

name: UTRAN-Vector
description: One UMTS authentication quintet: RAND, XRES, AUTN, cipher key CK, and integrity key IK, plus an optional Item-Number.

name: GERAN-Vector
description: One GSM authentication triplet: RAND, SRES, and ciphering key Kc, plus an optional Item-Number.

name: Network-Access-Mode
description: Says which core domains the subscription permits. Values are PACKET_AND_CIRCUIT (0) and ONLY_PACKET (2); value 1 is reserved.

name: HPLMN-ODB
description: Bit mask of home-network-specific barring categories set by the operator. Bits 0 to 3 correspond to HPLMN specific barring types 1 to 4, whose meaning is defined by the home operator; they may also apply to MO short messages.

name: Item-Number
description: A sequence number placed in each authentication vector so the receiver knows the order of vectors delivered in one answer.

name: Cancellation-Type
description: Why the HSS (or CSS) is cancelling a location in CLR. Values are MME_UPDATE_PROCEDURE (0), SGSN_UPDATE_PROCEDURE (1), SUBSCRIPTION_WITHDRAWAL (2), UPDATE_PROCEDURE_IWF (3), and INITIAL_ATTACH_PROCEDURE (4).

name: DSR-Flags
description: Bit mask in DSR that tells the MME or SGSN which parts of the stored profile to remove. Examples are Regional Subscription Withdrawal (0), Complete APN Configuration Profile Withdrawal (1), PDN subscription contexts Withdrawal (3, using Context-Identifier), STN-SR (4), Trace Data Withdrawal (8), CSG Deleted (9), and MSISDN Withdrawal (23).

name: DSA-Flags
description: Bit mask the SGSN returns in DSA. Bit 0 (Network Node area restricted) reports that the whole SGSN area is now off limits because of regional subscription.

name: Context-Identifier
description: A numeric identifier for one APN configuration or PDP context in the subscription. It names the default APN inside APN-Configuration-Profile and selects which contexts to delete in DSR.

name: Subscriber-Status
description: Whether service is granted or barred for the subscriber. Values are SERVICE_GRANTED (0) and OPERATOR_DETERMINED_BARRING (1); with the latter, the barring detail is in Operator-Determined-Barring.

name: Operator-Determined-Barring
description: Bit mask of operator determined barring categories. Bits cover all packet oriented services barred (0), roamer access to HPLMN or VPLMN access points (1, 2), and outgoing call barring variants such as all outgoing (3), international (4), and inter-zonal (6) calls.

name: Access-Restriction-Data
description: Bit mask where each set bit forbids a radio access type for the subscriber. Bits include UTRAN Not Allowed (0), GERAN Not Allowed (1), WB-E-UTRAN Not Allowed (4), HO-To-Non-3GPP-Access Not Allowed (5), NB-IoT Not Allowed (6), NR as Secondary RAT Not Allowed (8), LTE-M Not Allowed (11), and several satellite access bits.

name: APN-OI-Replacement
description: A dotted domain name that replaces the APN Operator Identifier when the serving node builds the full APN and the APN-FQDN for PGW DNS lookup, in non-roaming and home-routed cases. It can be set per UE or per APN.

name: All-APN-Configurations-Included-Indicator
description: Tells the receiver whether an APN configuration profile is complete or a delta. Values are All_APN_CONFIGURATIONS_INCLUDED (0) and MODIFIED_ADDED_APN_CONFIGURATIONS_INCLUDED (1).

name: APN-Configuration-Profile
description: The subscriber's set of EPS APN subscriptions. It holds one or more APN-Configuration entries, the Context-Identifier of the default APN (with extra defaults when non-IP or Ethernet APNs exist), and a flag saying whether the list is complete.

name: APN-Configuration
description: Subscription settings for one APN: its Context-Identifier, APN name, PDN type, default-bearer QoS, APN-AMBR, any static UE address or PGW identity, and options such as charging characteristics, LIPA/SIPTO permissions, and 5GS interworking.

name: EPS-Subscribed-QoS-Profile
description: The subscribed QoS for an APN's default bearer: a QCI and an Allocation-Retention-Priority. Only non-GBR QCI values may be sent over S6a/S6d.

name: VPLMN-Dynamic-Address-Allowed
description: Whether the UE may use a PGW in the visited network for this APN, or only one in the home network. Values are NOTALLOWED (0) and ALLOWED (1); absence means not allowed.

name: STN-SR
description: The Session Transfer Number for SRVCC, an E.164 number in TBCD digits that the MME uses to transfer an IMS voice call to the circuit-switched domain.

name: Alert-Reason
description: The reason given when reporting that a UE can receive short messages again. Values are UE_PRESENT (0) and UE_MEMORY_AVAILABLE (1).

name: AMBR
description: Aggregate maximum bit rate for uplink and downlink, used for the UE-AMBR or an APN-AMBR. Rates are in bit/s, with extended kbit/s fields used when the value is above the 32-bit limit.

name: CSG-Subscription-Data
description: One closed subscriber group the user belongs to: the CSG-Id, an optional expiry time, the APNs reachable via LIPA from that CSG, and optionally the PLMN it applies to (the registered PLMN when absent).

name: CSG-Id
description: The 27-bit Closed Subscriber Group identity as defined in 23.003, carried in an Unsigned32 with the unused low-order bits set to zero.

name: PDN-GW-Allocation-Type
description: Says whether the PGW identity in MIP6-Agent-Info was provisioned in the HSS or picked by the network. Values are STATIC (0) and DYNAMIC (1).

name: Expiration-Date
description: The time at which the user's membership of a CSG ends.

name: RAT-Frequency-Selection-Priority-ID
description: The subscribed Subscriber Profile ID for RAT/Frequency Priority (SPID), a value from 1 to 256 that the radio network uses to steer idle and connected mode camping.

name: IDA-Flags
description: Bit mask the SGSN returns in IDA. Bit 0 (Network Node area restricted) reports that the entire SGSN area is restricted by the regional subscription just inserted.

name: PUA-Flags
description: Bit mask the HSS returns in PUA. Freeze M-TMSI (0) and Freeze P-TMSI (1) ask the MME or SGSN not to reuse the purged UE's temporary identity right away.

name: NOR-Flags
description: Bit mask in NOR stating what the serving node is reporting. Bits include Single-Registration-Indication (0), Ready for SM from SGSN (2), UE Reachable from MME (3), Ready for SM from MME (6), Homogeneous Support of IMS Voice Over PS Sessions (7), S6a/S6d-Indicator (8), and Removal of MME Registration for SMS (9).

name: User-Id
description: The leading IMSI digits (MCC, MNC, and the start of the MSIN) as text. In a Reset it names a group of subscribers sharing that prefix.

name: Equipment-Status
description: The EIR verdict on a piece of mobile equipment. Values are PERMITTEDLISTED (0), PROHIBITEDLISTED (1), and TRACKINGLISTED (2).

name: Regional-Subscription-Zone-Code
description: One regional subscription Zone Code naming a set of tracking or routing areas in the visited network where the user may or may not roam. Up to ten may be given per VPLMN; the serving node works out the allowed areas.

name: RAND
description: The random challenge RAND sent to the UE as part of an authentication vector.

name: XRES
description: The expected response XRES that the network compares with the UE's answer to the challenge.

name: AUTN
description: The authentication token AUTN the UE uses to verify the network and check sequence freshness.

name: KASME
description: The EPS key K_ASME derived by the HSS for an E-UTRAN vector, from which the MME derives NAS and access stratum keys.

name: Trace-Collection-Entity
description: IPv4 or IPv6 address of the Trace Collection Entity that receives trace records for a subscriber or equipment trace session.

name: Kc
description: The GSM ciphering key Kc in a GERAN authentication triplet.

name: SRES
description: The signed response SRES expected from the SIM in a GERAN authentication triplet.

name: PDN-Type
description: The IP address type allowed for a PDN. Values are IPv4 (0), IPv6 (1), IPv4v6 (2, dual stack), and IPv4_OR_IPv6 (3), which permits either single stack but not dual stack and is used only in the subscription.

name: Roaming-Restricted-Due-To-Unsupported-Feature
description: Marks that roaming in the current network is restricted because the serving node lacks a feature the subscription needs. Its single value is Roaming-Restricted-Due-To-Unsupported-Feature (0).

name: Trace-Data
description: Activates a subscriber or equipment trace in the serving node. It carries the trace reference, depth, network element types, interfaces and events to record, the collection entity address, and optional MDT settings.

name: Trace-Reference
description: Identifies a trace session: the MCC and MNC of the PLMN followed by a 3-octet Trace ID, six octets in total.

name: Trace-Depth
description: How much detail the trace records, using the trace depth values of 32.422 (minimum, medium, maximum, and their vendor-specific variants).

name: Trace-NE-Type-List
description: Octet string, coded per 32.422, naming which network element types should run the trace.

name: Trace-Interface-List
description: Octet string, coded per 32.422, listing which interfaces the trace should record.

name: Trace-Event-List
description: Octet string, coded per 32.422, listing which events trigger trace recording.

name: OMC-Id
description: Identity of the operations and maintenance centre that should receive trace results, coded as in MAP.

name: GPRS-Subscription-Data
description: The subscriber's GPRS profile for an SGSN or combined node. It holds between one and fifty PDP-Context entries and a flag saying whether the list is complete.

name: Complete-Data-List-Included-Indicator
description: Says whether a set of PDP contexts is the full list or only changes. Values are All_PDP_CONTEXTS_INCLUDED (0) and MODIFIED_ADDED_PDP CONTEXTS_INCLUDED (1).

name: PDP-Context
description: One subscribed GPRS PDP context: its Context-Identifier, PDP type and optional static address, subscribed QoS, APN, plus options such as APN-AMBR, charging characteristics, LIPA/SIPTO permissions, and non-IP delivery settings.

name: PDP-Type
description: The PDP type of a subscribed context, coded as in MAP. Allowed values are IPv4 (0x21), IPv6 (0x57), and Non-IP (0x02).

name: 3GPP2-MEID
description: The Mobile Equipment Identifier of a 3GPP2 terminal, carried in place of an IMEI and encoded as the MEID octets defined by 3GPP2 A.S0022.

name: Specific-APN-Info
description: Used only under a wildcard APN configuration, it names a specific APN the UE has connected to and the PGW serving it, so the HSS can track dynamically allocated gateways for that APN.

name: LCS-Info
description: The subscriber's location services data: GMLCs in the home network allowed to request the UE's location, privacy exception classes (S6d only), and subscribed MO-LR classes.

name: GMLC-Number
description: The E.164 number of a GMLC, in TBCD digits, that may issue mobile terminated location requests for the UE.

name: LCS-PrivacyException
description: One LCS privacy exception class: the supplementary service code and its status, the notification rule, and the external clients, PLMN clients, or service types allowed to locate the UE.

name: SS-Code
description: A supplementary service code coded as in MAP, used to name LCS classes, call barring services, and similar services.

name: SS-Status
description: The provisioning and activation status of a supplementary service, coded as in MAP.

name: Notification-To-UE-User
description: How the user is told about a location request. Values are NOTIFY_LOCATION_ALLOWED (0), NOTIFYANDVERIFY_LOCATION_ALLOWED_IF_NO_RESPONSE (1), NOTIFYANDVERIFY_LOCATION_NOT_ALLOWED_IF_NO_RESPONSE (2), and LOCATION_NOT_ALLOWED (3).

name: External-Client
description: An external LCS client allowed to locate the UE for an MT-LR, with its identity, an optional GMLC restriction, and a notification rule.

name: Client-Identity
description: The E.164 number of an external LCS client, in TBCD digits.

name: GMLC-Restriction
description: Limits which GMLCs may relay a location request from a client. Values are GMLC_LIST (0) and HOME_COUNTRY (1).

name: PLMN-Client
description: A category of LCS client inside the PLMN that may locate the UE. Values include BROADCAST_SERVICE (0), O_AND_M_HPLMN (1), O_AND_M_VPLMN (2), ANONYMOUS_LOCATION (3), and TARGET_UE_SUBSCRIBED_SERVICE (4).

name: Service-Type
description: An LCS service type whose clients may locate the UE for an MT-LR, with an optional GMLC restriction and notification rule.

name: ServiceTypeIdentity
description: Numeric identity of an LCS service type, with values as defined in MAP.

name: MO-LR
description: One mobile originated location request class the UE subscribes to, given as a supplementary service code and its status.

name: Teleservice-List
description: The short-message teleservices the subscriber is provisioned with, given as one or more TS-Code values.

name: TS-Code
description: A teleservice code coded as in MAP, for example the short message MO-PP teleservice.

name: Call-Barring-Info
description: One call barring supplementary service that applies to short messages, given as its service code and status.

name: SGSN-Number
description: The E.164 ISDN number of an SGSN, in TBCD digits.

name: IDR-Flags
description: Bit mask in IDR asking the MME or SGSN for actions or data. Bits include UE Reachability Request (0), T-ADS Data Request (1), EPS User State Request (2), EPS Location Information Request (3), Current Location Request (4), Local Time Zone Request (5), Remove SMS Registration (6), and P-CSCF Restoration Request (8).

name: ICS-Indicator
